tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write

I removed the credit line from the landing page (bottom-left, "Neuron Cell Low-poly Simple by vitalik.kucha · CC BY 4.0", all three parts links). It was the only text on the page that linked anywhere. The page now shows just the name, the tagline and the sign-in button. The frontend still type-checks.

**This creates a licence problem.** That line was the credit the neuron model's CC BY 4.0 licence requires. With it gone, the 3D neuron is on screen with no credit anywhere the audience can see it. The licence file in `frontend/public/models/` is still there, but nobody at the expo will see it. Two ways to fix it:

- **Plain text:** bring the credit back with no links, in the same small faint style. This still meets the licence and doesn't look like a link.
- **Hover/info control:** put the credit behind a tiny ⓘ in the corner, so it's off the page until someone looks for it.

I haven't committed this; it's sitting with your other uncommitted changes to the landing page.

The frontend still type-checks, but I haven't looked at it in the browser. It's worth checking that the thin beam still stands out against the light background, since pale yellow on a light page can wash out. If it does, a slightly deeper yellow such as `#fbbf24` would fix it.

gh issue list                  # what's open

content.text:
Nothing is wrong with your main branch's history. It matches GitHub exactly: nothing ahead, nothing behind. The problem is one file, `docs/STATUS.md`, stuck half-merged after a stash didn't come back cleanly.

**What happened (from git's log of your recent actions):**
1. You were on main with an uncommitted 5-line "Done" entry in `docs/STATUS.md` about the landing rework.
2. You stashed it and pulled, which brought in PR #4.
3. You re-applied the stash. It conflicted, because PR #4 rewrote `STATUS.md` completely.

So the file now has conflict markers (`<<<<<<< Updated upstream` …) and git shows it as unmerged (`UU`). No merge or rebase is in progress; it's only this file.

**Why it won't merge:** PR #4 moved the task board to GitHub Issues. `STATUS.md` is now a "Findings" page with no "Done" section, so your entry has nowhere to go. It's also out of date, since it still says "amber glow" and the beam is now yellow.

**Nothing is lost:**
- Your landing page work is committed on `frontend/diagnosis` (commit `76dc1b3`) and pushed.
- Because the stash didn't apply cleanly, git kept it as `stash@{0}`.

**The fix** is to keep the new version from GitHub and drop your old entry:

```bash
git checkout HEAD -- docs/STATUS.md   # take the pulled version, clears the conflict
git stash drop                         # throw away the stale Done entry
```

To keep a record of the landing rework, put it in a comment on the GitHub issue for it, now that tasks live there.

Do you want me to run those two commands?

content.text:
The home page (`/home`) now uses the same background as the landing page, at the same strength. It had been using a fainter version: the characters were at 55% of the landing's opacity and the colour gradient at 35%. Both now match the landing (80% and 60%).

- **`frontend/src/pages/Home.tsx`:** the background no longer asks for the fainter version.
- **`frontend/src/components/background.tsx`:** I removed the fainter option, since nothing else used it. Both pages now share one fixed look.

I didn't copy the landing's white fade to the home page. That fade is placed to sit behind the name and sign-in button at the bottom right, and the home page has nothing there.

The frontend type-checks, but I haven't looked at it in the browser. The stronger pattern could make text harder to read wherever it sits on the background with no card behind it, like the page titles and descriptions. If it's too busy, I can bring back a slightly fainter setting for the home page only.

===== PAGE 7 =====
Alex Chen 
Alex is 47. He has taught senior biology at a high school on the Hamilton mountain for
nineteen years, writes everything on the whiteboard and walks the rows while students
work. He coached cross-country for a decade and ran half-marathons until the spring of
2025.
He lives in Westdale with his partner Jordan, a medical radiation technologist on 7 am to 4
pm shifts, and their two children, Maya, 16, and Leo, 14. In June 2024 a student asked
whether his marker had run dry. His handwriting had started to fade out halfway across the
board. The marker was fine. He waited a few months, then saw his family doctor. What
follows is his file. 
Mountain Brow Family Health Team 
Hamilton, Ontario
Referral
14 October 2024
Alex Chen, 45, male
To: Plastic and Hand Surgery Clinic 
Re: Right hand weakness and deteriorating handwriting, four months 
Thank you for seeing Alex, a 45-year-old right-handed teacher who is otherwise well. Since June he has
noticed that his handwriting fades across the page and that his right thumb and index finger tire quickly
when writing on a whiteboard. He has started dropping his whiteboard marker and his coffee cup. No pain.
No numbness or tingling. He reports some cramping in the right forearm at night.
On examination the right thenar eminence looks a little flatter than the left. Grip is slightly weaker on the
right. Phalen's test was equivocal. Sensation to light touch was normal in all fingers. He works at a desk in the
evenings marking, and I suspect a carpal tunnel syndrome or a median neuropathy at the wrist.
I would be grateful for your assessment and for nerve conduction studies at the wrist. He has no significant
past history, takes no medication, does not smoke and runs regularly. 
Dr. Priya Raman, MD, CCFP 
Family physician 
Plastic and Hand Surgery Clinic 
Consultation and follow-up. Dictated, not read.
Consultation 9 December 2024
Follow-up 21 April 2025
Alex Chen
Copy to: Dr. P. Raman 
Re: Query right carpal tunnel syndrome 
Consultation.   Six months of right hand weakness affecting fine tasks, no sensory symptoms. Nerve
conduction across the right wrist: median sensory and motor latencies within normal limits; no slowing
across the carpal tunnel. Visible wasting of the right thenar muscles and the muscle between thumb and
index finger. Grip 4 out of 5 on the right. Given the thenar wasting, his occupational demands and his wish to
try something, I offered a right carpal tunnel release as a reasonable trial of treatment. He elected to
proceed after discussion of the risks and the uncertain benefit. Surgery 20 January 2025, uncomplicated. 
Follow-up, three months after surgery.   Wound well healed. He reports no improvement. If anything the
hand is weaker, and he now notices twitching under the skin of the forearm, which he describes as "rippling".
He has also begun to mention his right foot catching on stairs. I have no further surgical options to offer.
Returned to the care of his family physician with a suggestion that a neurological opinion may be helpful if
symptoms progress. 
Dr. Marcus Oyelaran, MD, FRCSC 
Plastic and reconstructive surgery 
BioHacks 2026   7 
===== PAGE 8 =====
Westdale Physiotherapy and Sports Clinic 
Discharge summary
10 February 2026
Alex Chen
12 August 2025 to 5 February 2026, 18 sessions
To: Dr. P. Raman 
Re: Right foot drop, treated as peroneal weakness. Not improving. 
Alex was referred in August 2025 for a right foot that catches on curbs and slaps on landing. He had
stopped running in May because the right leg "felt heavy and would not do what I asked". A lumbar
spine MRI in December 2025 was reported as unremarkable for his age, with no nerve root compression.
Over six months of strengthening, balance work and a trial of an off-the-shelf ankle brace, his right
ankle dorsiflexion has gone from 4 out of 5 to 3 out of 5. Calf and thigh circumference on the right are
each about 2 cm smaller than the left. He now uses a cane outside the house. He reports two falls, both
in the evening, one on the stairs at home and one leaving the school at dusk. He has stopped cycling to
work and drives instead.
Three things concern me. The weakness is progressing despite treatment. His reflexes are brisk,
including at the right ankle, which is not what I would expect from a peripheral nerve problem. And he
mentions that his right hand has been weak for well over a year and that a wrist operation did not help
it. I do not think this is an ankle problem. I would strongly recommend a neurology referral, and I have
told Alex so. 
Daniela Ferreira, PT, MScPT 
Registered physiotherapist 
Mountain Brow Family Health Team 
Hamilton, Ontario
Referral, marked urgent
16 February 2026
Alex Chen, 46, male
To: Neurology, outpatient clinic 
Re: Progressive painless weakness, right arm and leg, twenty months 
I would be grateful if you could see Alex soon. I first saw him in October 2024 with right hand weakness
that I referred as a carpal tunnel syndrome. His wrist studies were normal, a carpal tunnel release in
January 2025 did not help, and in the past year he has developed a right foot drop that physiotherapy
has not improved and that a lumbar MRI does not explain.
Today he reports muscle cramps, visible twitching in both forearms and lately the right thigh, and that
he has lost about 6 kg without trying since the summer. His voice is unchanged as far as he is aware,
although his partner says he is quieter in the evenings. There is no pain, no numbness, no change in
bladder or bowel function and no visual symptoms. On examination he has wasting of the right hand
and brisk reflexes in all four limbs. I am concerned about a progressive neurological condition and
would value your opinion. I am sorry this has taken as long as it has. 
Dr. Priya Raman, MD, CCFP 
BioHacks 2026   8 
===== PAGE 9 =====
Neurology Outpatient Clinic 
Consultation note. Neuromuscular service.
Seen 11 June 2026
Referral received 18 February 2026
Alex Chen, 47, male
Referring: Dr. P. Raman 
Reason for referral: progressive painless weakness, right arm and leg, now two years
History 
Right-handed, 47. First symptom June 2024: handwriting fading on the whiteboard, fatigue in the right
thumb and index finger. Right carpal tunnel release January 2025 after normal wrist studies, no benefit.
Right foot drop from spring 2025, progressing through physiotherapy; lumbar MRI unremarkable.
Cramps in both calves and the right forearm, worse at night. Fasciculations noticed in the forearms
since April 2025, now also in the right thigh. Unintentional weight loss, 86 kg two years ago to 78 kg
today.
On direct questioning: speech is clear in the morning but his partner and students notice slurring by late
afternoon, which he had put down to tiredness. Occasional coughing when drinking water quickly. He
has started sleeping on two pillows because he feels "short of air" lying flat. No diplopia, no sensory
symptoms, no sphincter change. Mood is low but he denies hopelessness. He is still teaching full time
and still drives.
Family history: no neurological disease in parents, siblings or grandparents. No dementia. Social: lives
with partner and two teenagers, non-smoker, two drinks a week. No toxin exposure. 
Examination 
General.   Thin. Weight 78 kg. Normal cognition in conversation, but on a bedside screen he produced
only nine words beginning with the same letter in one minute, with intact memory and orientation. 
Cranial nerves.   Eye movements full. Face symmetric. Tongue shows mild wasting with fasciculations at
rest. Jaw jerk brisk. Palate elevates symmetrically. Speech mildly spastic in quality late in the
consultation, intelligible. 
Upper limbs.   Marked wasting of the right thenar eminence and first dorsal interosseous, with relative
sparing of the hypothenar muscles. Fasciculations in both forearms and the right deltoid. Tone
increased on the right. Power: right grip 4/5, right finger abduction 3/5, right thumb abduction 3/5, left
upper limb 5/5. Reflexes brisk and symmetric, right more than left. Hoffmann sign present on the right. 
Lower limbs.   Right calf wasting. Fasciculations in the right quadriceps. Tone increased bilaterally. Power:
right ankle dorsiflexion 3/5, right hip flexion 4/5, left lower limb 5/5. Reflexes brisk, with three beats of
clonus at the right ankle. Right plantar response extensor, left flexor. 
Sensation.   Normal to light touch, pinprick, vibration and proprioception throughout.   Gait.   Right foot
drop with a high-stepping gait and a cane. Unable to walk on heels on the right. Romberg negative. 
Investigations requested 
Nerve conduction studies and needle electromyography, four regions. MRI brain and cervical spine.
Bloods as per neuromuscular panel. Pulmonary function tests upright and supine. Referral to speech-
language pathology. Review in four weeks with results. 
Dr. Hannah Weiss-Okafor, MD, FRCPC 
Neurologist, neuromuscular disease 
BioHacks 2026   9 
===== PAGE 10 =====
Electromyography Laboratory 
Nerve conduction studies and needle EMG

Alex Chen
Requested by: Dr. H. Weiss-Okafor

Widespread active denervation and chronic reinnervation in four body regions, including clinically

Dr. Hannah Weiss-Okafor, MD, FRCPC

Alex Chen

Diagnostic Imaging 
MRI brain and cervical spine, with and without contrast
16 June 2026
Alex Chen
Requested by: Dr. H. Weiss-Okafor 
Clinical information: progressive upper and lower limb weakness with brisk reflexes. Exclude cord
compression. Query motor neuron disease. 
A. Brain, axial FLAIR   at the level of
the internal capsule. Symmetric
hyperintensity along the posterior
limb of the internal capsule on
both sides (arrows), following the

- Bilateral, symmetric corticospinal tract signal change and a motor band sign. These findings are
supportive of a degenerative process affecting the upper motor neurons in the appropriate clinical

- No structural lesion of the brain or cervical cord to account for the patient's weakness. Specifically, no
cervical spondylotic myelopathy, no demyelinating lesion, no mass.
- No abnormal enhancement after contrast, so nothing to suggest tumour, infection or inflammation. 
Dr. Thanh Nguyen, MD, FRCPC

===== PAGE 13 =====
Neurology Outpatient Clinic 
Letter to referring physician. Copy given to the patient at his request.
14 July 2026
Alex Chen, 47, male
To: Dr. P. Raman 
Diagnosis: amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), limb onset, with early bulbar and respiratory
involvement 
Dear Dr. Raman,
I saw Alex and his partner Jordan today to go through his results, and I am sorry to say that the
diagnosis is ALS. I spent the appointment with them and the clinic social worker, and they will return in
two weeks to talk further. He asked that this letter be written in plain language and that he be given a
copy, which I have done. 
How the diagnosis was made.   ALS is diagnosed on the clinical picture, not on any single test. Alex has
progressive weakness with signs of both upper motor neuron damage (brisk reflexes, clonus, a
Hoffmann sign, an upgoing plantar, spastic speech) and lower motor neuron damage (wasting,
fasciculations, low motor amplitudes, denervation on EMG) in the same regions, now spread across all
four: bulbar, cervical, thoracic and lumbosacral. Sensation is normal. The MRI excludes the structural
conditions that can mimic this, the bloods exclude the treatable ones, and the EMG shows the process
is active and widespread. He meets the Gold Coast criteria without ambiguity. In retrospect he probably
met them a year ago.

import type { Patient } from './pipeline'

/**
 * Pull the structured patient profile out of a case file's text. Clinical
 * letters repeat facts as they change (age 45 → 47, FVC 78 → 76), so for
 * anything that evolves we take the LAST mention, which is the most recent.
 * Anything the file doesn't state is left as "Not stated", never guessed.
 */

const NOT_STATED = 'Not stated'
const PROVINCES = 'Ontario|Quebec|British Columbia|Alberta|Manitoba|Saskatchewan|Nova Scotia|New Brunswick|Newfoundland and Labrador|Prince Edward Island|ON|QC|BC|AB|MB|SK|NS|NB|NL|PE'

const last = (text: string, re: RegExp) => [...text.matchAll(re)].at(-1)
const sentence = (s: string) => s.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + s.slice(1)

export function parseCasePatient(pages: string[]): Patient {
  const t = pages.join('\n').replace(/\s+/g, ' ')

  // "Alex Chen, 45, male" … "Alex Chen, 47": the name and the latest age.
  const people = [...t.matchAll(/\b([A-Z][a-z]+ [A-Z][a-z]+), (\d{1,3})\b(?:,? (male|female))?/g)]
  const name = people[0]?.[1] ?? 'Uploaded patient'
  const mentions = people.filter((m) => m[1] === name)
  const age = Number(mentions.at(-1)?.[2] ?? NaN)
  const sexWord = mentions.find((m) => m[3])?.[3]
  const sex = sexWord === 'male' ? 'M' : sexWord === 'female' ? 'F' : ''

  const onset = t.match(/\b(limb|bulbar|spinal|respiratory)[ -]onset\b/i)?.[1]
  const weeks = last(t, /(\d+) weeks? (?:from|since) diagnosis/gi)?.[1]
  const months = last(t, /(\d+) months? (?:from|since) diagnosis/gi)?.[1]
  const alsfrs = last(t, /ALSFRS-R:? (\d{1,2}) ?(?:of|\/) ?48/g)?.[1]
  const slope = t.match(/decline of (?:about )?([\d.]+) points? (?:per|a) month/i)?.[1]
  // Digits can't be skipped between "vital capacity" and the value, so a table title can't borrow a later number.
  const fvc = last(t, /vital capacity[^.\d]{0,40}(\d{2,3})(?: and \d{2,3})? per ?cent/gi)?.[1]

  const panel = t.match(/Genetic panel:? (.+?) (No pathogenic variant detected|Pathogenic variant detected[^.]*)/i)
  const genes = panel?.[1].replace(/ repeat expansion/g, '').replace(/ and (\d+) further genes/, ' + $1 more')
  const genetics = panel ? (/^no/i.test(panel[2]) ? `Panel negative (${genes})` : `${panel[2]} (${genes})`) : NOT_STATED

  const med = t.match(/Medication:? ([A-Z][^.]+?)(?: since [^.]*)?\./)?.[1]
  const medications = med ? [med] : /takes no medication/i.test(t) ? ['None'] : [NOT_STATED]

  const place = t.match(new RegExp(`\\b([A-Z][a-z]+), (${PROVINCES})\\b`))
  // What the patient has turned down or is hoping for, in the file's own words.
  const preferences = [...t.matchAll(/[^.]*\b(?:declined|[Ww]ants to|[Ww]ould like to)\b[^.]*\./g)]
    .map((m) => sentence(m[0].trim().replace(/^(?:He|She|They) (?:has |have )?/, '').replace(/\.$/, '')))
    .filter((s) => s.length <= 90)
    .slice(0, 4)

  return {
    id: name.split(' ').map((w) => w[0]).join(''),
    label: name,
    age,
    sex,
    onset: onset ? `${sentence(onset.toLowerCase())} onset` : 'Onset not stated',
    monthsSinceDx: weeks ? Math.round(Number(weeks) / 4.345) : Number(months ?? NaN),
    alsfrs: Number(alsfrs ?? NaN),
    slope: slope ? -Number(slope) : NaN,
    fvc: Number(fvc ?? NaN),
    genetics,
    medications,
    comorbidities: /no significant past history/i.test(t) ? [] : [NOT_STATED],
    location: place ? `${place[1]}, ${place[2]}` : NOT_STATED,
    coverage: NOT_STATED,
    preferences,
    fusEligible: false,
  }
}

import type { Patient } from './pipeline'

/**
 * Pull the structured patient profile out of a case file's text. Clinical
 * letters repeat facts as they change (age 45 → 47, FVC 78 → 76), so for
 * anything that evolves we take the LAST mention, which is the most recent.
 * Anything the file doesn't state is left as "Not stated", never guessed.
 */

const NOT_STATED = 'Not stated'
const PROVINCES = 'Ontario|Quebec|British Columbia|Alberta|Manitoba|Saskatchewan|Nova Scotia|New Brunswick|Newfoundland and Labrador|Prince Edward Island|ON|QC|BC|AB|MB|SK|NS|NB|NL|PE'

const last = (text: string, re: RegExp) => [...text.matchAll(re)].at(-1)
const sentence = (s: string) => s.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + s.slice(1)

export function parseCasePatient(pages: string[]): Patient {
  const t = pages.join('\n').replace(/\s+/g, ' ')

  // "Alex Chen, 45, male" … "Alex Chen, 47": the name and the latest age.
  const people = [...t.matchAll(/\b([A-Z][a-z]+ [A-Z][a-z]+), (\d{1,3})\b(?:,? (male|female))?/g)]
  const name = people[0]?.[1] ?? 'Uploaded patient'
  const mentions = people.filter((m) => m[1] === name)
  const age = Number(mentions.at(-1)?.[2] ?? NaN)
  const sexWord = mentions.find((m) => m[3])?.[3]
  const sex = sexWord === 'male' ? 'M' : sexWord === 'female' ? 'F' : ''

  const onset = t.match(/\b(limb|bulbar|spinal|respiratory)[ -]onset\b/i)?.[1]
  const weeks = last(t, /(\d+) weeks? (?:from|since) diagnosis/gi)?.[1]
  const months = last(t, /(\d+) months? (?:from|since) diagnosis/gi)?.[1]
  const alsfrs = last(t, /ALSFRS-R:? (\d{1,2}) ?(?:of|\/) ?48/g)?.[1]
  const slope = t.match(/decline of (?:about )?([\d.]+) points? (?:per|a) month/i)?.[1]
  // Digits can't be skipped between "vital capacity" and the value, so a table title can't borrow a later number.
  const fvc = last(t, /vital capacity[^.\d]{0,40}(\d{2,3})(?: and \d{2,3})? per ?cent/gi)?.[1]

  const panel = t.match(/Genetic panel:? (.+?) (No pathogenic variant detected|Pathogenic variant detected[^.]*)/i)
  const genes = panel?.[1].replace(/ repeat expansion/g, '').replace(/ and (\d+) further genes/, ' + $1 more')
  const genetics = panel ? (/^no/i.test(panel[2]) ? `Panel negative (${genes})` : `${panel[2]} (${genes})`) : NOT_STATED

  const med = t.match(/Medication:? ([A-Z][^.]+?)(?: since [^.]*)?\./)?.[1]
  const medications = med ? [med] : /takes no medication/i.test(t) ? ['None'] : [NOT_STATED]

  const place = t.match(new RegExp(`\\b([A-Z][a-z]+), (${PROVINCES})\\b`))
  // What the patient has turned down or is hoping for, in the file's own words.
  const preferences = [...t.matchAll(/[^.]*\b(?:declined|[Ww]ants to|[Ww]ould like to)\b[^.]*\./g)]
    .map((m) => sentence(m[0].trim().replace(/^(?:He|She|They) (?:has |have )?/, '').replace(/\.$/, '')))
    .filter((s) => s.length <= 90)
    .slice(0, 4)

  return {
    id: name.split(' ').map((w) => w[0]).join(''),
    label: name,
    age,
    sex,
    onset: onset ? `${sentence(onset.toLowerCase())} onset` : 'Onset not stated',
    monthsSinceDx: weeks ? Math.round(Number(weeks) / 4.345) : Number(months ?? NaN),
    alsfrs: Number(alsfrs ?? NaN),
    slope: slope ? -Number(slope) : NaN,
    fvc: Number(fvc ?? NaN),
    genetics,
    medications,
    comorbidities: /no significant past history/i.test(t) ? [] : [NOT_STATED],
    location: place ? `${place[1]}, ${place[2]}` : NOT_STATED,
    coverage: NOT_STATED,
    preferences,
    fusEligible: false,
  }
}

import { test } from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { parseCasePatient } from './case-patient.ts'

// Lines lifted verbatim from the BioHacks 2026 hacker package (Alex Chen's file),
// one string per page, as pdfjs extracts them.
const ALEX = [
  'Mountain Brow Family Health Team Hamilton, Ontario Referral 14 October 2024 Alex Chen, 45, male To: Plastic and Hand Surgery Clinic',
  'He has no significant past history, takes no medication, does not smoke and runs regularly.',
  'Genetic panel: C9orf72 repeat expansion, SOD1, TARDBP, FUS and 28 further genes No pathogenic variant detected Reported 30 July 2026 Forced vital capacity, sitting 78 per cent of predicted Above 80 per cent',
  'Diagnosis: amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), limb onset, with early bulbar and respiratory involvement',
  'Alex Chen, 47 27 months from first symptom, 10 weeks from diagnosis Medication Riluzole 50 mg twice daily since July. Tolerating. Edaravone declined for now.',
  'ALSFRS-R 32 of 48 (bulbar 9, fine motor 6, gross motor 7, breathing 10). Decline of about 0.6 points per month since onset, roughly linear.',
  'Forced vital capacity, sitting and lying flat 76 and 61 per cent of predicted',
  'ALSFRS-R and vital capacity over time (892 records), drawn from 12 per cent of trials.',
]

test("parses Alex Chen's case into the latest values", () => {
  const p = parseCasePatient(ALEX)
  assert.equal(p.label, 'Alex Chen')
  assert.equal(p.age, 47) // the later letter, not the 2024 referral
  assert.equal(p.sex, 'M')
  assert.equal(p.onset, 'Limb onset')
  assert.equal(p.monthsSinceDx, 2)
  assert.equal(p.alsfrs, 32)
  assert.equal(p.slope, -0.6)
  assert.equal(p.fvc, 76) // latest sitting value; the dataset blurb must not leak in
  assert.equal(p.genetics, 'Panel negative (C9orf72, SOD1, TARDBP, FUS + 28 more)')
  assert.deepEqual(p.medications, ['Riluzole 50 mg twice daily'])
  assert.deepEqual(p.comorbidities, [])
  assert.equal(p.location, 'Hamilton, Ontario')
  assert.equal(p.coverage, 'Not stated')
})

test('leaves what a file does not say as not stated, never invented', () => {
  const p = parseCasePatient(['A one-line note with nothing clinical in it.'])
  assert.ok(Number.isNaN(p.age))
  assert.ok(Number.isNaN(p.alsfrs))
  assert.ok(Number.isNaN(p.fvc))
  assert.equal(p.genetics, 'Not stated')
  assert.equal(p.location, 'Not stated')
})

The patient case page (`/home/case`) now asks for the PDF and fills in Alex Chen's details from it. The new parser reads every field correctly from your hacker package, the frontend type-checks, and the parser's tests pass. I haven't uploaded the PDF through the browser, so the full flow on screen still needs a click-through.

**What the page shows now:**
- **Heading:** "00 · Patient profile — Upload the patient profile.", with a line explaining that the PDF is read in the browser and turned into the profile the agents use.
- **Before upload:** just the drop zone and the **Run patient analysis** button, which stays greyed out until a PDF is added.
- **After upload:** the PDF preview on one side and the patient card on the other, filled in from the file.
- The Goal card, the criteria switches and the "Sample patient" note are gone. The goal and criteria keep their default values in the background, so the rest of the pipeline is unchanged.

**What it reads from your PDF:**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Patient | Alex Chen, 47M |
| Onset | Limb onset, about 2 months since diagnosis (the file says "10 weeks") |
| ALSFRS-R | 32/48, falling about 0.6 points a month |
| FVC | 76% predicted |
| Genetics | Panel negative (C9orf72, SOD1, TARDBP, FUS + 28 more) |
| Medication | Riluzole 50 mg twice daily |
| Location | Hamilton, Ontario |

Where the file gives a value more than once, the parser takes the latest one: 47 not 45, FVC 76 not 78. Anything the file doesn't state, like insurance coverage or other conditions, shows as "—", "Not stated" or "None recorded" rather than a made-up value. The "MRgFUS eligible" badge no longer appears, because nothing in the case file states eligibility.

The parsed patient also feeds the agent activity log on the analysis page, the report and the saved-runs list.

**Still from the old sample patient:** two of the scripted drug profiles and candidate notes in `src/lib/pipeline.ts` (lines 94 and 187) still mention CKD stage 2, which Alex doesn't have. A judge reading the report could catch that, so it's worth fixing before the demo; tell me if you want it changed.

**Files:**
- `src/lib/case-patient.ts` — the new parser.
- `src/lib/case-patient.test.ts` — its tests; run them with `node --test src/lib/case-patient.test.ts`.
- `src/lib/case-pdf.ts` — attaches the parsed patient to the uploaded file.
- `src/components/discovery/pages.tsx` and `pieces.tsx` — the case page and the patient card.
- `src/components/discovery/runs.tsx` and `src/lib/run-store.tsx` — use the parsed patient instead of the sample one.
